summary.title: Toren
summary.pov: Third-person limited (focalized through Toren Voss), with occasional shifts in focus to Rook and Dessa during critical tactical moments. The narrative voice is immediate but grounded in physical sensation.
summary.synopsis: The group attempts a defensive ambush at Hallam Cross against a 'Verge-hound' using the terrain (revetments) as an anchor for Rook's power. Toren misinterprets the creature's behavior based on prior training, nearly killing Wyck and himself before Dessa decodes the enemy's true mechanics: stillness indicates engagement, not disengagement.
summary.openingState: Tense preparation; high stakes established by Senna Voss warning Rook about his mortality. The group is physically compromised (Wyck injured, Pitch shaking).
turningPoints: The ambush begins with the flyover collapse and the creature's emergence.
Rook creates a 'wall of nothing' to stop the initial charge.
Toren misreads the feint: he assumes stillness means disengagement (standard hound behavior) but steps into the path of the rear legs, which are actually the primary weapon in this specific instance.
Wyck is thrown; Rook creates a second wall to save him at great personal cost (bleeding internally).

Dessa identifies the rule reversal: 'The thing that goes quiet is the thing that isn't coming.' The creature drops its blade-limb to fire its legs. Toren realizes his training was inverted for this specific enemy.
Toren successfully strikes the root of the limb, but the creature retreats on three legs rather than dying.
summary.closingState: Exhaustion and grim realization. The group is severely injured (Rook bleeding internally, Wyck broken collarbone/wrist, Toren's hand damaged). They must travel four miles to Meridian in open pasture at first light against a creature that hunts by sensing Rook's power.

characters.name: Toren Voss
characters.function: Focalizer/Combatant. Struggles with the failure of his training and must unlearn instinctual reactions to survive.
characters.vocalBehavior: Internal monologue is analytical but increasingly frantic; dialogue becomes clipped, breathless, or declarative as he processes new data.

characters.name: Rook
characters.function: Leader/Power User. Physically failing (internal bleeding) but mentally sharp and protective.
characters.vocalBehavior: Low register, authoritative but fraying at the edges; uses short commands ('NOW', 'Say it back'). His voice carries a heavy physical weight.

characters.name: Dessa Cole
characters.function: Observer/Analyst. The only one who sees the pattern clearly.
characters.vocalBehavior: Flat, precise, and rhythmic; devoid of panic even when screaming Wyck's name once. Her voice is a tool for decoding reality.

characters.name: Wyck Tanner
characters.function: Anchor/Support. Physically broken but mentally resilient.
characters.vocalBehavior: Quiet, continuous swearing; physical pain limits his ability to speak loudly or commandingly.

locations: Hallam Cross: A defensive position with eleven concrete revetment blocks and a collapsed flyover. The terrain is flat open pasture beyond the embankment.
The Gap: An eleven-foot space between blocks used as an ambush point.
terms: Verge-hound (or 'Hound'): A creature with four limbs, one of which can transform into a blade-limb. It uses stillness to signal engagement.
Barrel: A massive entity made of ash; the enemy type that has learned they are vulnerable.
The Road/Nothing: Rook's power creates an invisible barrier ('piece of nothing') that stops physical force.
summary.actionCadence: Starts slow and deliberate (preparation), accelerates into chaotic, sensory-overload violence (the attack), slows to a tense pause for analysis (Dessa's realization), then shifts to a grim, methodical debrief.
summary.emotionalRegister: High-stakes survival; the transition from fear to confusion to cold clarity. Undercurrent of grief and exhaustion regarding Senna Voss's warning about funerals.
narrationRisks: The tactical explanation by Dessa ('It drops one to pick up the other') must not be rushed or flattened into a lecture; it requires rhythmic precision as she is decoding physics, not just shouting facts.
Toren's internal realization of his error ('That was backwards') needs a distinct shift in cadence from panic to cold horror. Do not overact this; let the silence carry the weight.
The description of Rook's injury (blood appearing) should be delivered with matter-of-fact gravity, avoiding melodrama.
carryForward: Rook is critically injured and cannot hold a road again for three days. He must walk four miles at first light.
The enemy ('Barrel') has learned they can hurt the group; it will hunt them by sensing Rook's power from miles away.
Toren knows how to kill the creature now but is physically limited (hand injury) and lacks a weapon capable of killing it in open ground without support.
